claim: For an agent to achieve information entropy reduction in scientific discovery, the system must be an open system that exchanges information with the physical world, because internal uncertainty cannot decrease in an isolated system.
falsifier: One could test whether an agent that receives no external physical feedback (isolated system) fails to reduce its internal uncertainty, while an agent that can query the physical world (open system) shows decreasing entropy over time.

conditions: the agent aims to reduce information entropy in scientific discovery
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported theoretical framework and hypothesized conditions; transfer beyond the described information-theoretic model is unestablished.

title: Operating as an open–information entropy reduction mechanism

claim: Prompting a language model to generate intermediate answer decompositions before final attributions improves attribution performance in a single forward pass.
falsifier: On a held-out attribution benchmark, compare attribution accuracy of a language model prompted to first generate a decomposition versus one prompted to produce attributions directly, controlling for model and task.

exclusions: limited to the language models, tasks, and evaluation settings reported in the study

title: Generating answer decompositions as for attribution performance

claim: In cooperative multi-agent environments, the performance improvement from using conventions becomes more pronounced as the number of agents increases, and convention-augmented agents exhibit robustness to increased player counts.
falsifier: In a cooperative multi-agent environment (e.g., Hanabi), train agents with and without convention-augmented action spaces for different numbers of players (e.g., 2, 3, 4, 5). Measure final performance and variance to test whether the performance gap widens with more agents and whether convention-augmented agents show less variance across player counts.

conditions: agents are trained with Rainbow DQN
the environment is Hanabi with varying numbers of players (2–5)
conventions are appended to the primitive-action space
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported system, task (Hanabi), population (Rainbow agents), and player counts tested; transfer beyond them is unestablished.
